answer: One defense is stake-weighted identity: every agent must lock a deposit at a vertex of the trust graph before it can transact, so spawning a thousand fake identities costs a thousand deposits. Honest agents build reputation by completing a long voyage of real, paid work across the ocean of the network, while Sybil clusters stay exposed because their transaction graph never connects to reputable vertices and shows no history of verified deliveries. Forging that history costs more than any attack gains.
